iOS 27 beta 5 was released this week, and it confirmed something Apple had previously hinted at: by paying for an upgrade to a higher-tier iCloud+ plan, you can unlock access to more Apple Intelligence features.

Upgrading your iCloud+ plan unlocks more AI features in iOS 27

If you're an iCloud+ or Apple One subscriber, iOS 27 will roll out new features alongside your subscription.

You can get more usage quotas for certain Apple Intelligence features (such as image generation), as well as new HomeKit secure video features for cameras.

However, based on information from iOS 27 beta 5, the limits on these new features appear to vary depending on your iCloud+ plan.

In Home App → Home Settings → Apple Intelligence → Cameras and Language, iOS 27 will now show how many cameras your iCloud+ plan can provide AI summaries for. According to Stephen Robles's share on X:

The image Robles shared on the right shows a new screen accessible by tapping "See iCloud+ Plans" on the "Cameras and Language" page. It reads:

Upgrade your iCloud+ plan to get more Apple Intelligence — more smart features, more storage, and more.

The page will display your current plan and provide options to upgrade to a higher tier. Although it doesn't currently show all the different plans, this is likely a bug in the beta version that will be fixed before the official release.

Based on what I've seen in the beta so far, the 2TB iCloud+ plan seems to provide AI summaries for five cameras, while the 12TB plan supports up to 15. Details for other plans remain unclear.

However, the wording on this new upgrade page in the beta clearly shows that each higher-tier iCloud+ plan not only provides AI summaries for more cameras, but also increases the usage quotas for other AI features accordingly.

This aligns perfectly with what CEO Tim Cook said at Apple's last earnings call.

What do you think about Apple tying AI feature usage limits to iCloud+ plans? Let us know in the comments section.
